stories.title: “Get Lit” Livestream, 4:30 pm ET: Episode One, William Faulkner’s “As I Lay Dying”
stories.text: Illustrated by Daniel Medina Get Lit continues today with William Faulkner’s As I Lay Dying, a novel that, far more even than Cash Bundren’s coffin above, involves a significant amount of craftsmanship. The story of a dead matriarch and her family’s 40-mile journey of dubious necessity to bury her is told through fifteen narrators across over sixty sections. The means are unconventional, the end controversial, and Brad and I will discuss it this afternoon, hopefully with many of you. Join us at 4:30 PM ET at: Substack Rumble YouTube You can also find us on X, @mtaibbi or @waywardrabbler . See you soon!

stories.title: A Graham Platner Write-In Campaign Might End Up Helping Troy Jackson
stories.text: A bubbling effort by a small group of Graham Platner’s supporters in Maine to write the former Senate candidate’s name on the ballot in November has begun to attract online attention, as Cheyenne Hunt, the Democratic operative who crusaded against Platner, has publicly denounced the possibility. “Platner supporters are posting in a private Facebook group, reporting back on their conversations with him. Allegedly, Platner himself has ‘endorsed’ the write-in strategy laid out here,” Hunt wrote . “This final act of hubris and selfishness would only help Collins win in November.” Collins is of course Sen. Susan Collins, who Democratic nominee Troy Jackson will face in November. Jackson replaced Platner on the ballot after Platner dropped out in July following a rape allegation that was brought to Politico and CNN by Hunt . Drop Site is always free to read. One of the organizers of the campaign to write in Platner’s name, Scott Niemi, published an oped about it in the Bangor Daily News; a Portland Press-Herald columnist has denounced the effort ; and a New York Post reporter has reached out to the people involved. stories.author: Bellingcat
stories.title: Investigating a Murder: Public Records Uncover New Clues in Chinatown Cold Case - bellingcat
stories.text: On a June night in 1996, in a basement apartment in Boston’s Chinatown, a killer put a pistol to the back of a young man's head and pulled the trigger.

stories.author: Bellingcat team
stories.title: Investigating a Murder: Public Records Uncover New Clues in Chinatown Cold Case
stories.text: The victim’s body was wrapped in quilts, lowered into the trunk of a car and driven about 20 miles southwest of the city, where it was dumped in the woods. It lay undiscovered through two New England winters until a dog walked home carrying a human bone. For three decades, authorities did not release the victim’s name to the public. He is listed in the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NamUs) as #UP12385, one of 202 unidentified people recorded in the state of Massachusetts. The circumstances of his discovery are reduced to five words: “Skeletal remains found in woods.” The case remains unsolved. Bellingcat spent more than a year investigating in an effort to put a name to the victim. Using open sources, including freedom-of-information requests and newspaper archives, as well as interviews with investigators who worked on the case, we pieced together the story of the man’s life and death in an era before the internet kept a digital record. In total, we submitted 27 public records requests to 18 local, state and federal law enforcement agencies. We also contacted more than two dozen investigators, prosecutors, crime victims, journalists, experts and community groups

stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: Trump Labor Secretary nominee pitched access to “America’s comprehensive welfare” to Chinese nationals
stories.text: Keith Sonderling in China (Flickr.com, ks3106) Acting Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling, who has been nominated by Trump to permanently lead the department, is a member of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud. In that role, Sonderling has pledged to “ root out waste, fraud, and abuse ” in safety net programs like unemployment insurance “and protect hardworking Americans’ tax dollars.” Prior to joining the Trump administration, however, as an attorney at the Florida law firm Gunster , Sonderling had a much different relationship with these programs. During two trips to China in 2015, Sonderling made numerous speeches and presentations pitching Chinese nationals on investments in Florida. These events were designed to entice potential Chinese investors by emphasizing that their investment would make their entire family eligible for green cards, allowing them to live and work permanently in the United States through a controversial program known as EB-5. At a July 2015 presentation Sonderling delivered with the Premier Capital Group, a Chinese language banner in the room emphasized that investors who received green cards would have access to “America’s Comprehensive Welfare.”

stories.title: He Champions Centrist Dems On Cable. He Also Works For Big AI.
stories.text: This is a collaboration with The American Prospect , a magazine about ideas, politics, and power . Max Rose, the pugnacious former Democratic congressman from Staten Island, has been a frequent guest on cable news this election cycle, touting the success of moderate candidates in this year’s Democratic primaries like Luke Bronin in Connecticut’s First Congressional District and Cait Conley in New York’s 17th District. “These are each instances of phenomenal public servants, phenomenal records… It’s do you have new ideas, are you willing to shake up the system,” said Rose, a self-described “old-school Democrat,” during a recent appearance on MSNOW. These candidates have something else in common: They were lifted to success over progressive opponents with millions of dollars in spending from VoteVets, an influential veteran-focused political network where Rose serves as a top adviser. Rose, an Army veteran, joined the organization by 2024 after a stint in the private sector following his unsuccessful 2020 reelection bid.
